conventions.commits: Conventional commits with scope, e.g. 'feat(core): add Swift language support with tree-sitter-swift handler (#1742)' (commit dbc2971). Commit bodies carry 'Signed-off-by: Hugues Clouatre' (DCO). The issue requires GPG-signed commits too; I did not verify signatures in history.
conventions.testing: Inline #[cfg(test)] mod tests at the bottom of each languages/*.rs file, using tree_sitter::Parser, Query::new and QueryCursor (java.rs, swift.rs, css.rs, kotlin.rs). Table-driven registry test in languages/mod.rs. Extension tests in lang.rs. Integration tests in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ use common::call_tool_raw and tempfile::NamedTempFile::with_suffix_in.
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings -W clippy::cognitive_complexity (ci.yml line 137); workspace lints deny unwrap_used, expect_used (test code exempt via cfg_attr) and undocumented_unsafe_blocks; cargo deny check advisories licenses bans (ci.yml line 211); REUSE compliance.
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option<String> or Vec<String> and never Result; source slicing is guarded with end <= source.len() (java.rs) or get_node_text (mod.rs); query compile failures surface as ParserError::QueryError from parser.rs; unsupported languages fall back to an unsupported-language error.

patterns: Each languages/<lang>.rs exposes pub const ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY as r"..." strings plus optional handler fns; mod.rs maps them into LanguageInfo with Some(...) or None per slot.

Element captures contract (parser_elements.rs 285-293): 'function' or 'class' on the outer node, with 'func_name' or 'method_name' and 'class_name' or 'type_name' for names; name fallback is child_by_field_name("name") on the function node.

enclosing_function_name (parser_elements.rs ~425-460) already matches "function_definition" and "method_declaration" by child_by_field_name("name"), so PHP needs no extract_function_name handler for enclosing-function lookups.

extract_inheritance is called with (class_node, source) for each class-like element (parser_elements.rs 398-402); Java emits 'extends X' and 'implements X'; Swift emits 'extends X' and 'conforms X' and guards on node.kind() first.

Java DEFUSE_QUERY lists write patterns before the (identifier) @read.usage catch-all, and extract_def_use skips reads at offsets already recorded as writes (parser_elements.rs ~880-890), so pattern order matters.
css.rs is the minimal template: ELEMENT_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY only, an empty CALL_QUERY const, and every handler slot None in mod.rs.
fortran.rs is the precedent for defuse_query: None (mod.rs), so the defuse slot can be omitted without a compile error.

Every language is registered in four places: workspace Cargo.toml, core Cargo.toml, lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP, and mod.rs (pub mod, get_language_info, get_ts_language); lang.rs supported_languages() is also hand-maintained.

constraints: The issue states the maintainers implement it in-house and external PRs will be closed; this scout output is internal guidance only.
Use LANGUAGE_PHP, not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY: the php_only grammar test parses bare 'echo' without <?php tags (bindings/rust/lib.rs tests), so it cannot satisfy the HTML-mixed acceptance criterion.
bindings/rust/build.rs compiles both php/src and php_only/src parser.c and scanner.c, so the binary size delta is expected to be larger than a single-grammar language.

cargo deny requires new Cargo.lock entries to be at least 7 days old (AGENTS.md). GitHub release v0.25.2 is dated 2026-11-19T16:26:36Z, which is 8 days before the clone date; the crates.io publish date was not verified (no crates.io access). Fallback: v0.25.1 (2026-10-06).

tree-sitter-php 0.25.x depends on tree-sitter-language 0.1 and dev-depends on tree-sitter 0.27; the lock already has tree-sitter 0.27.2 and tree-sitter-language 0.1.9, so no version conflict is expected.

Scope limits from the issue: no extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver or find_receiver_type; no trait use resolution; no property or constant extraction; no attributes; no namespace alias import; no .phtml, .inc, .module or .php5 extensions; no tool handler or schema change.

DEFUSE_QUERY is optional at the type level (defuse_query: Option<&str>) and the parser only errors when it fails to compile. Its inclusion is required by the issue Scope and acceptance criteria, not by the compiler. extract_def_use has no production caller since the symbol tool removal (parser_elements.rs comment at line ~841), so it is exercised only by tests.
The issue requires the five query constants and extract_inheritance in php.rs, so a DEFUSE-less build would miss an acceptance criterion even though it compiles.
Workspace lints deny unwrap_used and expect_used outside test code, and clippy runs with -W clippy::cognitive_complexity in CI.
test_coverage: languages/java.rs, swift.rs, css.rs and kotlin.rs each have inline tests that compile their queries and check captures (element, import, call, defuse). java.rs tests extract_inheritance for extends and implements. kotlin.rs has the most thorough coverage (element, call, import, inheritance, defuse, receiver functions). languages/mod.rs has a registry table test (test_get_language_info_covers_remaining_registered_languages) that includes css and yaml rows, and lang.rs tests language_for_extension, including an ECMAScript pattern check over EXTENSION_MAP. No existing integration test in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ targets a specific language other than Rust (*.rs NamedTempFile in analyze_file_structured_content_tests.rs and analyze_module_structured_content_tests.rs). The PHP work therefore needs one new integration file plus inline tests in php.rs.

approaches.name: A: Full Java/Swift-pattern integration (recommended)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class, interface, trait, enum), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression, member_call_expression, nullsafe_member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression), REFERENCE_QUERY ((named_type (name)) and (named_type (qualified_name))), IMPORT_QUERY ((namespace_use_declaration) @import_path), DEFUSE_QUERY (assignment, augmented, update, simple_parameter, static_variable_declaration, plus variable_name read), and extract_inheritance walking base_clause and class_interface_clause children. Use LANGUAGE_PHP. Wire the 4 registry places plus Cargo.toml, core Cargo.toml, lock, lang.rs supported_languages, README.
pros: Meets every acceptance criterion in the issue, including the five query constants and extract_inheritance.
Mirrors java.rs and swift.rs, so reviewers can check it line by line.
Every node kind and field name used is confirmed in node-types.json.
The HTML-mixed edge case is covered by LANGUAGE_PHP.
cons: Largest test surface: five queries to compile, plus inheritance, defuse and integration tests.
DEFUSE_QUERY has no production consumer, so it is exercised only by tests.
Binary size grows because build.rs compiles both grammars.

approaches.name: B: Minimal core (elements, calls, imports only)
approaches.description: Follow css.rs and fortran.rs: ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY only, with defuse_query: None and extract_inheritance: None in mod.rs. Wire the same registry places.
pros: Smallest change, with the fewest query compile risks.
Fortran shows defuse: None is an accepted pattern.
cons: Fails acceptance criteria: no DEFUSE_QUERY, no extract_inheritance, so extends and implements are not reported.
Leaves the Java/Swift parity the issue asks for undone.

approaches.name: C: Grammar tags.scm-derived queries with a parity check
approaches.description: Start ELEMENT_QUERY and CALL_QUERY from the grammar's own queries/tags.scm patterns (function_definition, method_declaration, class, interface, trait, function_call_expression, scoped_call_expression, member_call_expression), renaming their captures (@name, @definition.*, @reference.*) to the aptu-coder contract (@function, @class, @func_name, @class_name, @call). Add the enum pattern by hand, since none appears in the first 40 lines of tags.scm. Use the tags.scm inheritance pattern for the class_interface_clause walk.
pros: Reuses patterns the grammar maintainers test, so they may track grammar changes better.
tags.scm also captures object_creation_expression as a reference, which could feed REFERENCE_QUERY.
cons: Capture names differ from the repo contract, so each pattern needs renaming and retesting.
tags.scm was not read in full, so an enum or other gap may exist.
Does not remove the need for the hand-written DEFUSE_QUERY, which tags.scm does not cover.

recommendation: Approach A. The issue's acceptance criteria require all five query constants, extract_inheritance with a specified output format, the HTML-mixed edge case and one integration file, and only A meets them. Use LANGUAGE_PHP. Take the element and call patterns from tags.scm as a cross-check (approach C), but keep the aptu-coder capture names. Confirm the crates.io publish date of tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 against the 7-day cargo-deny rule before pinning; fall back to 0.25.1 if needed. Keep DEFUSE_QUERY in scope because the issue requires it, even though it has no production consumer.

Element query draft: covers function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration and enum_declaration (all six named declaration kinds in node-types.json with a name field). Excluded: anonymous_function and arrow_function (closures, not named declarations), enum_case (enum member, not a declaration kind in the issue).
defuse_query_draft:
(assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name) @write.assign))
(augmented_assignment_expression left: (variable_name (name) @writeread.assign))
(update_expression argument: (variable_name (name) @writeread.update))
(simple_parameter name: (variable_name (name) @write.param))
(static_variable_declaration name: (variable_name (name) @write.static))
(variable_name (name) @read.usage)

Adapted from java.rs DEFUSE_QUERY. PHP has no typed local_variable_declaration, so the write sites are assignment_expression.left, augmented_assignment_expression.left (writeread), update_expression.argument (writeread), simple_parameter.name and static_variable_declaration.name, all of which are fields confirmed in node-types.json. The read catch-all is restricted to variable_name children rather than all identifiers, because PHP names (function, class, method) are 'name' nodes. Write patterns must stay ABOVE the read catch-all: parser_elements.rs (~line 880-890) skips read captures at byte offsets already recorded as write/writeread, which depends on match order. Captures include only the 'name' child, so the symbol text compared in extract_def_use is 'y', not '$y'. global_declaration is omitted because its variables are not a named field in node-types.json.
inheritance_walk_citation:
Grammar source inspected: tree-sitter-php repo, php/src/node-types.json (305 types) and php/grammar.js (defineGrammar('php')), whose rules live in common/define-grammar.js.
Rule for class_declaration (common/define-grammar.js lines ~365-373): seq(optional(field('attributes', $.attribute_list)), repeat($._modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)), optional($.base_clause), optional($.class_interface_clause), field('body', $.declaration_list)).
Rule for base_clause (lines ~334-337): seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name)). No field name is attached to base_clause.
Rule for class_interface_clause (lines ~381-384): seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name)). No field name is attached to class_interface_clause.
Rule for _name (line ~296): choice(alias(keyword('static', false), $.name), alias(choice(...CAST_TYPE_CLASS_NAMES...), $.name), reserved('classes', $.name), $.qualified_name, ...).
node-types.json for class_declaration: fields = {attributes, body, name} ONLY; children = [abstract_modifier, base_clause, class_interface_clause, final_modifier, readonly_modifier, static_modifier, var_modifier, visibility_modifier]. There is NO 'superclass' or 'interfaces' field, unlike java.rs which calls child_by_field_name("superclass") and child_by_field_name("interfaces").
node-types.json for base_clause: fields = {}; children = [name, qualified_name, relative_name].
node-types.json for class_interface_clause: fields = {}; children = [name, qualified_name, relative_name].
FIELD-WALK (proposed extract_inheritance for class_declaration node N): (1) for each child C of N (iterate by kind, not by field) where C.kind() == "base_clause": for each named child X of C where X.kind() in {name, qualified_name, relative_name}: push format!("extends {text(X)}"). (2) for each child C of N where C.kind() == "class_interface_clause": for each named child X of C where X.kind() in {name, qualified_name, relative_name}: push format!("implements {text(X)}"). (3) return in source order. Expected output for 'class Foo extends Bar implements A, B {}': ["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]; for 'class Plain {}': []. Enum: enum_declaration also has class_interface_clause (implements only), and a primitive_type child for the backing type, which must be skipped. Interface: interface_declaration has base_clause (extends, multiple names) and no class_interface_clause. The tags.scm query in the same repo (queries/tags.scm) uses (class_interface_clause [(name) (qualified_name)] @name) as the same pattern, which corroborates this walk.
